conventions.convention: Natural units c=ℏ=1; Minkowski metric diag(-1,1,1,1); orientation dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³; trivial bundles and smooth compactly supported backgrounds and transformation parameters.
Positive chirality means eigenvalue +1 of γ₅=iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³. The identification of this convention with Bilal's is defective; see concerns.
D=d+iB; B transforms to B+dα, the charge-one field to exp(-iα)ψ, and θ to θ-α. Thus B+dθ and G=dB are invariant.

Use the consistent effective-action anomaly, Z=exp(iΓ), and no non-invariant local counterterm. The adopted threshold relation is Γ_H=F_M[B+dθ,M_H]-Δ_M, with invariant F_M and measure multiplier exp(-iΔ_M).

E/M_H≪1 concerns a specified finite-leg background vertex, not Fourier support of compactly supported fields; the local anomaly identity is independent of this condition. No global anomaly, continuum construction, or quantitative remainder is claimed.

This is a formal perturbative input about local variation and mass independence, not a construction of the full determinant.

concerns.concern: The Definition sets γ₅=iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³=-iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃ and says this matches “Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention in Eq. (2.20).” Bilal actually defines γ₅=iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃=-iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³, the negative of the item's operator. This is explicit in the source HTML, Eq. (2.20): https://arxiv.org/html/0802.0634v1#S2.E20, and is independently consistent with Eq. (10.14), whose four-dimensional factor is i³=-i. Thus the selected +1 eigenspace is Bilal's negative-chirality space. The claimed source identification is false and is load-bearing for the anomaly sign.

Statement and Proof 1.2 identify γ₅=+iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ with Bilal's positive-chirality matrix and apply his negative-coefficient Hermitian anomaly formula. Bilal Eq. (2.20) instead uses -i times the upper-index product; §§8 and 9.3 explicitly attach the quoted anomaly formula to his positive-chirality field. With the item's Clifford/chirality convention retained, its field has the opposite source chirality, reversing the source-derived triangle anomaly and Wess–Zumino coefficient. The algebra after adopting A1 is correct, but adopting that formula does not make its claimed source/chirality identification faithful. Check Bilal Eqs. (2.20), (9.30), (10.14) at https://arxiv.org/html/0802.0634v1.

The geometric computation ∫αG∧G=2 is correct, but the claimed positive variation +1/(12π²) inherits the theorem's source/chirality sign mismatch. If the presently defined γ₅=+iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³ and +1 charged eigenspace are retained and Bilal's coefficient is translated faithfully, the variation has the opposite sign. This consumer needs explicit review when the upstream chirality/coefficient convention is resolved.

alerts.finding: The Definition fixes “γ₅=iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³=-iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃” and calls this “Bilal's mostly-plus positive-chirality convention, Eq. (2.20).” Bilal's actual Eq. (2.20) is γ₅=iγ₀γ₁γ₂γ₃=-iγ⁰γ¹γ²γ³; see https://arxiv.org/html/0802.0634v1#S2.E20. Eq. (10.14) also gives -i times the upper-index product in four dimensions. Consequently the item's positive-chirality eigenspace is the opposite source chirality, while its adopted source-normalized anomaly law is attributed to positive chirality without this sign conversion. This shared defect propagates into batch 44.
